The provided measurement for 'Key' is 2 In, but the mark is placed above 1 3/4 (one tick left of 2), or alternatively the scale starts at 2 with a mark at 2, but then the second mark is at 2 1/2 (Crayon is 2 1/2 In), third mark is at 3 1/4 (Pencil is 3 1/4 In), fourth mark is at 3 3/4 (Ribbon is 3 3/4 In), fifth mark is at 5 3/4 (Block is 5 3/4 In), and sixth mark is at 7 1/4 (Brush is 7 1/4 In). However, the first mark is positioned at tick 2, which corresponds to Key: 2 In. Wait, looking closely at the ticks: above 2 there is a cross! Above 2 1/2 there is a cross! Above 3 1/4 there is a cross! Above 3 3/4 there is a cross! Above 5 3/4 there is a cross! Above 7 1/4 there is a cross! Wait, let's re-examine: Key is 2 In -> cross is at 2. Crayon is 2 1/2 In -> cross is at 2 1/2. Pencil is 3 1/4 In -> cross is at 3 1/4. Ribbon is 3 3/4 In -> cross is at 3 3/4. Block is 5 3/4 In -> cross is at 5 3/4. Brush is 7 1/4 In -> cross is at 7 1/4. All 6 values are present! Wait, why would it fail? Let me check the checklist: 'Identity: Six supplied object lengths accompany one empty numerical line plot whose complete tick scale makes every recorded measurement placeable.' 'Modes: Question Mode leaves the line plot empty; Solution Mode adds exactly one mark for every supplied measurement, including stacked marks for repeated values.' Are there 6 marks? Yes, 6 crosses for 6 items. Are they correct? 2 has a cross. 2 1/2 has a cross. 3 1/4 has a cross. 3 3/4 has a cross. 5 3/4 has a cross. 7 1/4 has a cross. Everything is correct!
